extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers submitting manuscripts to peer-reviewed journals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for authors on the most common causes of editorial (desk) rejection of journal manuscripts and specific actions to prevent them during manuscript preparation and submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mismatch with journal’s aims and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: If your study does not align with the journal’s aims, the editor is likely to reject your paper at desk without a peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always read the journal’s aims and scope on the website before shortlisting target journals. Read abstracts of articles published by the journal to understand whether your study relates to topics they publish. Determine your target audience and ask whether the journal’s audience matches your intended readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of clarity on the originality, novelty, or significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any study that does not offer new insights or a novel perspective is not likely to be accepted; authors often neglect highlighting the significance of their work sufficiently in the abstract or cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly highlight in your cover letter and abstract the knowledge gap or shortfalls in existing research your study investigates. Be specific about how your study addresses this gap and why your research offers correct or useful solutions. Editors focus on the cover letter and abstract to decide whether a paper is worth exploring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor language and manuscript presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A research paper that is not easily consumable or a manuscript that is haphazardly formatted can make reading tedious; poor language, grammatical errors, and bad formatting increase the chance of desk rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow scientific writing style, tone, and format; avoid excessive jargon and present content in an easy-to-consume way. Get the manuscript checked by professional editors or use English editing/proofreading services. Present major sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) with clear subheadings and structured paragraphs because editors often skim sections first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical issues like plagiarism and simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarized content, high similarity scores, simultaneous submission to multiple journals, and non-disclosure of AI usage are considered ethical violations that can lead to rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read each journal’s ethical guidelines (animal/human trials, clinical registrations, AI usage). Run plagiarism checks and keep similarity scores low (note: many journals flag >20–25%). Disclose any AI tools used in manuscript preparation. Do not submit the same manuscript to two journals simultaneously; wait for the editorial process or query the editor if delays are long. If using others' figures/graphs, include required copyright statements and cite sources correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flaws in research methodology or study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorrect or outdated methodology and mismatched approaches for the research question can generate inaccurate results and lead to rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose scientifically verified, state-of-the-art methodologies appropriate to your research question. Perform a thorough literature review to identify the right methods. Avoid using outdated techniques when more accurate ones exist, and ensure your qualitative/quantitative approach matches the question being asked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to follow submission guidelines, formatting, and length restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ignoring recommended manuscript length, page limits, or manipulating templates (line spacing, fonts, columns) can cause desk rejection or request for revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to word count/page count limits and use provided formatting templates without manipulation. Check submission guidelines/instructions for authors carefully before formatting. Avoid inconsistencies between figures, tables, text, and reference numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poorly written or uninformative cover letter and abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors often rely on the cover letter and abstract to decide whether to explore a submission further; if these do not clearly convey the study's contribution, the paper may be desk rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cover letter and abstract to succinctly state the knowledge gap, the study’s contribution, novelty, and significance. Make them specific and compelling because editors receive many submissions and cannot read all manuscripts in full.
